analyst.summary: Tenneco Clean Air India makes emission-control and powertrain components for auto OEMs as part of the global Tenneco group, and generates outstanding returns on capital (ROE ~40%, ROCE ~58%) on a debt-free balance sheet. The catch is that revenue growth has been modest for several years (roughly 4-10% annually), while the stock trades at a growth-stock-like ~37x earnings. We rate it a Hold: an excellent business, but priced well above what its actual growth rate would typically justify.
